title: Parallel thoughts — interview runbook and quick calibration
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal runbook to structure notes during screens and panel debriefs. Not a formal scorecard — more of a mental checklist and a place to drop fragments I don't want to lose between back-to-back loops.

Context / when to use:
- Use in live screens when I'm the primary interviewer or shadowing.
- Use immediately after the interview to capture impressions before the panel meets.
- Feed distilled bullets into the canonical scorecard later (one-liner + 3 evidence points).

High-level mental model (what matters for runtime team):
- Systems maturity: observability, failure modes, graceful degradation.
- Performance thinking: latency budgets, batching, KV cache semantics.
- Runtime engineering instincts: memory/KV cache eviction strategies, memory layout tradeoffs.
- Trade-off literacy: knows what to optimize and what to leave alone.
- Communication: explains assumptions, asks clarifying Qs, surfaces unknowns.

Live-note checklist (short tags I can tick in my head):
- [ ] Clarifying questions asked early? (yes/no)
- [ ] Starts from a constraint-driven approach (latency/cost)?
- [ ] Mentions concrete measurements or experiments?
- [ ] Has prior infra experience shipping production rollouts?
- [ ] Can explain a subtle failure mode and mitigation?

Red flags (fast heuristics):
- Fixates on model architecture tricks without systems context.
- Vague on observability (no metrics/logs/traces plan).
- No examples of pragmatic trade-offs under pressure.
- Claims breadth but can't walk through a single system they own end-to-end.

Green flags / signal examples:
- Describes a recent incident, concrete timeline, root cause and postmortem changes.
- Talks about per-token cost optimizations with numbers or experiments.
- Designs a fallback strategy in a few minutes that covers SLOs and UX tradeoffs.
- Comfortable sketching a rollout plan including canary metrics, error budgets, and rollback thresholds.

Sample prompts & follow-ups to probe depth:
- "Imagine latency spikes when cold-starting KV cache — how do you detect and contain it?"
- "How would you measure end-to-end tail latency for a composite pipeline with caching? What synthetic tests and production signals?"
- "Give me a real example where you chose a worse-performing but more stable option — why?"
- "Walk me through your last postmortem — what surprised you, and what changed?"

Pairing exercise sketch (30 min):
- Small prompt: design an autoscaling policy for a dedicated GPU pool serving two models with different latency SLAs.
- Ask candidate to outline metrics, thresholds, cooldowns, and a fallback when capacity hits limit.
- Expected artifacts: short bullet list of metrics, a diagram or text flow showing routing, and a brief rollout checklist.

How I capture evidence (to paste into scorecard later):
1) One-line verdict (support/weak/neutral/reject) — keep it clean.
2) Strength bullets (2–3 short lines with specific examples).
3) Risk bullets (2 lines: where they'd need ramp and what to check in probation).

Example of a filled micro-entry (template):
- Verdict: support (conditional)
- Strengths: solid incident writeup (reduced p99 by isolating cache miss storm), concrete cost-savings experiment (switching quantization reduced 20% cost for same perf on short contexts).
- Risks: limited infra ownership for >1 year, unfamiliar with our trace/obs stack (needs onboarding).

Immediate todo after each loop:
- Email panel with 1-sentence summary and 2 follow-up questions for the candidate (if any).
- Drop 3 evidence bullets into the hiring doc within 24h.
- If big unknowns, ask hiring-owner to schedule follow-up deep-dive.

Open questions for calibration with Marco/Priya:
- Do we prefer concrete quantification for cost-saving claims (must cite numbers) or is well-structured thought process enough?
- Is there a standard probation checklist we should reference in risk bullets? (link to onboarding checklist would be helpful)

Notes-to-self (short):
- Try to keep the runbook <1 page; panel prefers concise evidence.
- When in doubt, default to asking for examples (past behavior beats hypotheticals).
- Remember to record any confounding context (candidate had interrupted prior week, candidate mentioned non-production project).

Quick follow-up templates (copy/paste helpers):
- To candidate: "Thanks for your time — quick follow-up: could you share a link to the incident postmortem you mentioned (or a short writeup)? It'd help the panel."
- To panel: "My take: support (conditional) — see 3 bullets. Main concern: onboarding on obs stack. Recommend 1-week technical take-home focused on CD/obs scenario.

Last-minute hacks when panel is split:
- Request a focused take-home targeted to the biggest gap (e.g., an ops-runbook + small infra change).
- Ask for a 30-min follow-up focused on the unknown area rather than re-scoring everything.

Scratch logs (quick raw captures) — dump here and prune later:
- 2025-02-12 10:03 — candidate mentioned they implemented an LRU-K variant; asked for numbers, gave ranges 30–60ms extra for eviction under heavy write rates. Follow-up: ask for a link or test sketch.
- 2025-02-12 10:47 — felt candidate leaned too academic when pressed on rollouts. Good mental model but lacked concrete canary metrics.

End of runbook.
Plain language, low friction. Keep iterating based on panel calibration notes.
